brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.write
objective.description: Patch one existing matter, apply terminal semantic value add/remove operations, and optionally update its brique-managed substance.

#root.role: Merge metadata patches, optionally write inline or leased substance data, and commit the updated matter revision.

matter_id._comment: Required. Name of the matter to write within the addressed context.

meaning._comment: Optional. Replacement for the meaning descriptor section.

functional._comment: Optional. Replacement for the functional descriptor section.

brique._comment: Optional. Replacement for the brique descriptor section.

semantic_patch._comment: Optional. Terminal semantic value operations: { add: [{path: string[] (array of key segments, e.g. ['functional','tags','domain']), value: any}], remove: [{path: string[], value: any}] }. path is always a JSON array of strings, never dot-notation. add creates missing parent objects and list leaves; remove deletes matching terminal values and prunes empty generated containers. path[0] MUST be one of the matter.json descriptor root sections — objective, subjective, functional, brique — or the whole call fails with reason=invalid_patch; no operation is applied when any op in the same call has an unrecognized root. semantic_patch can never reach matter substance/data — there is no path, however phrased, that touches data.bin. To change the matter's business content (a transcript, a document body, any payload), use params.data (full inline replacement) or an HTTP upload lease, never semantic_patch.

data._comment: Optional. Inline substance payload. Strings become raw bytes; other values are JSON-marshaled. How matter.read later serializes this content (plain string vs base64) is controlled separately by brique.substance_type ('text', the default, or 'binary') — set it via the 'brique' param above if this data is arbitrary binary content, or matter.read will hand it back as an unencoded string.

http_data._comment: Optional. Set to true to request an HTTP upload lease instead of writing inline substance data. When true, the engine opens a write lease and returns an http_data handle in the response; the caller must then PUT the bytes to the lease URL before it expires. Accepted values: true (bool), 'true' or '1' (string), non-zero number.

revision._comment: New revision number after the write. Present on inline write path.

http_data._comment: Present only when params.http_data was true. HTTP write lease handle: { kind: 'http', base_url: string, path: string (e.g. '/substance/<rid>'), rid: string, tok: string, expires_at: integer (unix nanoseconds), revision: integer, method: 'PUT' }. The caller must PUT the substance bytes to <base_url><path> before expires_at to complete the write. When present, revision is not included in the response (it is committed after the upload completes).

effects.matter_substance: data.bin may be replaced inline or via an HTTP lease when the matter stays in brique mode.
effects.subscriptions: Local brique subscribers may be notified after a successful commit.

transformation_contract.morphing: A matter identifier plus metadata or substance patches becomes a new committed matter revision, or an upload lease when the write is deferred through HTTP.
invariants: matter.write targets exactly one existing cataloged matter designated by matter_id.
semantic_patch.add and semantic_patch.remove operate only on terminal values; add creates missing object parents and list leaves, remove deletes matching values and prunes empty generated containers.
Payload bytes are writable only when the addressed matter remains in brique substance mode.
success: A successful direct write returns ok=true, matter_id, and the committed revision.
A successful deferred write returns ok=true, matter_id, and an HTTP upload lease handle in http_data.
failure: The capacity fails when matter_id is missing, no patch intent is provided, or a patch payload has the wrong shape.
The capacity fails when payload writing is requested outside brique mode or when the commit boundary cannot be completed.
The capacity fails with reason=invalid_patch, and applies none of the requested operations, when any semantic_patch op's path[0] is not one of objective, subjective, functional, brique.
notes: metadata patches are merged minimally into matter.json; semantic_patch is add/remove over terminal value leaves.
Subscription notifications happen only after a successful committed write in brique mode.
